$comment: The casing grade looks (CG2, ticket 830; GD lock of 24 Oct 16:28 on casing grades by depth, Progression's row): one plate metal per grade, keyed on the grade q alone. The plate is plates[(q - 1) mod 5], five authored metals each with its own tint, groove, rivet colour and rivet pattern, so neighbouring grades never match and a grade reads without colour (#48 acceptance 5, #51's casing row). The finish is finishes[floor((q - 1) / 5) mod F], cycled as #577's tail cycles its finishes, and the pips count the laps of that cycle, floor((q - 1) / (5 F)), drawn up to pips.most as bright dots in the seam: the uncapped tail. Every length is in tiles (one tile is one metre); the plate depth, ribs, seam and rivet geometry stay CASING_LINING_LOOK's (constants/scene.ts, ticket 315). Hazard lining trims (casing_cement types, #366) layer on the plate's seam by lining type id, so a ring shows its strength grade and its lining type at once. Plate colours sit above 0.62 luma so every plate stands a step from every band rock at phone size (casingLiningLook.test.ts); the colours and patterns are Progression's rows to retune, the rule never changes for a colour. Data rows only: no economy number lives here.
